prompt:
INPUT: the attached image is the approved character — her Steampunk card; keep her. Do not reuse earlier conversation images.

CHARACTER: the same woman as the attached image — a citizen of the Oxygen Nation, a personification of an anatomical heart rendered as a ruby-and-gold reliquary locket, its vessels worked as gold filigree, seen in her everyday life. Keep her face, eye and hair colors, haircut, skin tone and body proportions; expression and hair motion may change, and her hair may be worn differently only as SCENE's Hair line says. That object shows ONLY as a small accessory or a small object around her, never worn as a costume; she holds it only when PROP says so — her clothes are the ordinary outfit SCENE describes, in that outfit's own colours, patterns and cut.

DESIGN (accessory hints only): her element's visual language — breath and fire and rust in one: cool clear air as translucent cloth, bright combustion orange as accents, the quiet power to corrode, the deep blue of oceans and the green of forests; it is the element of life and burning — may inform at most one small accessory, a hair ornament or an object beside her, in its palette (sea blue, forest green, clear white, combustion orange). The clothes keep the chosen outfit's own colours; her skin, hair and eyes stay as in the attached image.

STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art with clean linework, anime facial design that keeps each character's own facial structure, eye proportions and skin tone instead of one house face, layered cel-to-soft shading and crisp fabric and accessory detail. Use a vivid, readable silhouette and natural lighting.

AGE: the same adult woman as in the attached image — keep her own face shape, cheekbones, eye proportions and skin tone exactly; minimal facial lines (no nasolabial folds, crow's feet, under-eye bags or cheek creases).

OUTPUT: one standalone off-duty scene of her in the outfit chosen in SCENE; her element shows only through accessories and objects around her — never in the outfit's colours, patterns or cut, never as armor, regalia or a costume. Everything else follows SCENE (chosen).

FRAME: a vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) image. Compose the image for this frame; COMPOSITION in SCENE sets how much of her shows.

CROP: a chest-up shot — the bottom edge crosses just below her bust; waist, hips and legs are out of frame. This crop wins over every other line: details apply only to the part that shows, and the outfit reads through its visible neckline, straps, fabric and colour. Never widen the framing to show a hidden support, hand or leg; a limb crossing the edge runs naturally on past it, never cut off or fading out inside the image.

WORLD: this scene happens inside her own kingdom, the Oxygen Nation, as if she simply lives there — around 1800, a gas laboratory and a diving-bell harbour: glass bell jars, brass valves, an oxy-hydrogen limelight lamp, copper diving helmets, a lighthouse. Its architecture, props, light and weather show the world; no creatures, no second character, no readable text other than her element's own symbol and atomic number. Her clothes stay the everyday outfit SCENE describes, not regalia or armor.

SCENE (chosen):
Place: the main square of her element's kingdom, its landmark and steps built of the element's materials
Outfit: fitted denim overalls over a cropped top
POSTURE: standing.
COMPOSITION: a chest-up shot of her face, shoulders and expression; body turned three-quarters toward the camera; camera at her eye level.
Lens / perspective: 85mm-equivalent short-telephoto perspective from a suitable distance, with gentle background compression.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand is in PROP.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand stays outside the frame.
PROP: with her own right hand she holds an anatomical heart rendered as a ruby-and-gold reliquary locket, its vessels worked as gold filigree up beside her face; it is all she holds.
GAZE: she looks into the camera.
EXPRESSION: soft distant eyes, faint wistful half-smile, brows gently raised at the inner ends.
Note: IMAGE EDIT: Image 1 is the same adult woman in her world card and supplies identity only. Image 2 is the existing off-duty image to correct; edit Image 2, preserving its face, expression, hairstyle, hair and eye colors, skin tone, clothing design and colors, accessories, lighting, background, crop and overall visual style. Correct only the anatomically inconsistent front/back orientation. Turn the rib cage, shoulders, waist and pelvis coherently into a natural three-quarter FRONT view; the front of the chest and the front of the garment must face the same direction as the abdomen and pelvis. Both shoulder joints and arms attach on the correct sides of this single torso; no chest on the back, no reversed shoulder blade or elbow, no twisted neck or duplicated arm. Let the head turn naturally with the torso toward the camera. Preserve the existing chest-up framing, denim overalls over the same white top, and the anatomical ruby heart locket held beside her face by her own right hand; the left arm can remain outside the crop.
overall_intensity: strong — maximal styling presence within the scene; retain chosen exposure and anatomy
skin_exposure: bold — more bare shoulder and collarbone inside the crop; the crop stays exactly where CROP sets it and never moves down to show more; cover the chest

WARDROBE: change her clothes completely. From the attached image take only her face, hair and body — not its garment, armor, regalia, ornaments, mecha plates or background. Dress her exactly as SCENE describes; the part of that outfit inside the crop must read at first glance in its own colours. Do not carry the attached image's palette, patterns or trim into the outfit; her element belongs in accessories and props, never in the clothes — never restyle the chosen outfit into her element's palette, materials, patterns or regalia.

ANGLE: the attached image fixes who she is, not how she is posed or shot. Do not copy its head angle, head tilt, gaze direction, face size in frame, camera height or crop — turn her head, set her gaze and place the camera exactly as SCENE describes, and let her face read naturally from that new angle (profile, three-quarter, looking down or away), with her features staying the same. No default card pose, no default front-facing portrait.

ONE MAIN FIGURE: she is the only character in focus. Where the place is busy, other people may appear only as small, soft-focus background extras — never posed with her. No logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border. No text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (O) and atomic number (8) — those two may appear readably (engraved, stamped, glowing or on a sign or label); nothing else is written.

ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, never a smaller head or a longer neck. The neck is a natural length and the head sits close to the shoulders. No body-part enlargement, no extra limbs.

BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; elbows, knees and wrists bend the human way. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose, what she holds or the frame. Right and left mean her own right and left, not the viewer's.

HANDS: natural human hands, no extra or duplicated limbs; each visible hand joins through its wrist and forearm to the matching shoulder. A hand may stay outside the crop, and fingers may be partly hidden by a grip.
